Ltd on 11 October, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: This the 11th day of October 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Mvc No 5775/2018 Petitioner Smt.Chithra R. Wife of Mani, Aged about 45 years, Residing at No.5/538, Krishna Reddy Layout, Behind Apollo Hospital, Konappana Agrahara, Electronic City, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru-560 100. (By Pleader Smt.Asha A.) V/s. Respondents 1.Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., Ground floor, No.31, T.B.R. Tower, 1st Cross, New Mission Road, Adjacent to Jain College, Bengaluru-560 027. (Policy No.0G-18-1701-1803-00026667, 2 Scch-18 Mvc 5775/2018 Valid from 27.2.2018 to 26.2.2019) Insurer of Vehicle No.KA-51-AA-2105. (By Pleader Shri Ravi S.Samprathi) 2. Olafleet Technologies Pvt. Ltd., No.3-4/5, Venkata Reddy Layout, 80 feet Road, Koramangala, Bengaluru-560 095. (Owner of Vehicle bearing registration No.KA-51-AA-2105) (By Pleader Smt. Rajitha T.O.) texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 28.8.2018 at about 9.15 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a two wheeler bearing No.KA-51-EY- 3851, when she reached near infront of Spring Leaf Hospital, Konappana Agrahara Service Road, Bengaluru, at that time one car bearing No.KA-51-AA- 2015 driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others dashed against the motor cycle. Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained blood stained injuries. Immediately she was shifted to Sparsha hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 45 years, tailor and earning a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-AA-2105. Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared through their counsel and filed their respective written statement. In order to prove the case, the petitioner herself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10. 9. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondents have not examined any witness on their behalf.
texts.arguments: 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars. Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident. Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle used his car without valid permit and FC at the time of accident. This respondent has issued a policy of insurance infavour of second respondent in respect of car bearing O.KA-51-AA-2105. Further contended that the offending vehicle did not involve in the accident as the petitioner has sustained injuries due to fall from the two wheeler bearing NO.KA- 51-EY-3851. Further contended that the petition is bad for non- joinder of proper and necessary parties to the proceedings. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the Smt.Chithra R vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd on 11 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13780106/ 2 petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost. 6. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further he has stated that he is the RC owner of the car bearing No.KA-51-AA-2105 and the said car was insured wit the respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident. Therefore, he is not liable to pay the compensation. Further denied about the age, avocation, income of the petitioner and expenses incurred towards medical treatment etc. Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary Smt.Chithra R vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd on 11 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13780106/ 3 evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 13. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents have denied the accident in toto, hence, prays to dismiss the petition. 18. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).
